question: Who arranged for Wallace to receive Darwin's book, and which dated letter records the arrangement?

claim.text: The letter headed CHARLES DARWIN TO A.R. WALLACE (November 13th, 1859) reports that its writer had told Murray to send its addressee the item described as “a copy of my book”.
qualifiers: The I/you/my bindings refer only to this documentary appearance; authorship is source-declared, not authenticated.
Reported instruction does not establish actual dispatch or receipt.
Heading date does not establish when the instruction, dispatch or receipt occurred.
Literal action/delivery qualification (exact scope unresolved): if possible
Additional hope stated by writer: I hope that you will receive it at nearly the same time with this note
Following source note retained without a separate historical claim: (N.B. I have got a bad finger, which makes me write extra badly.)

citations.quote: CHARLES DARWIN TO A.R. WALLACE. Ilkley, November 13th, 1859.

I have told Murray to send you by post (if possible) a copy of my book,
and I hope that you will receive it at nearly the same time with this
note. (N.B. I have got a bad finger, which makes me write extra badly.)
